clue.text: Their resting places have their points

definitions.text: Their resting places have their points

parts.words: Their resting places have their points
parts.note: the Egyptian kings of old were buried in pyramids, tombs that rise to a point

explanation.surface: A wry remark about people whose final homes are pointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' suggests opinions or arguments; here it means the peaks of the pyramids where the old rulers lie.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of ancient Egypt were entombed in pyramids, structures with pointed tops.

clue.text: Press for identity documents?

definitions.meaning: official documents proving who you are are your personal documents, as in 'show me your ___'

explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers make up the press, and official identification documents carry the same plural name.

clue.text: Is game playing a bias against the elderly?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of is game are moved about, in play

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a game is prejudiced against older players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like part of the game picture but is the anagram signal for 'Is game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination on the grounds of a person's years, typically against older people, is the sense.

clue.text: Sailor told to go on return watch for missing persons

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
someone told to go has been sent

indicators.note: on return means the word for watch comes back, read right to left

parts.note: to watch is to see

explanation.surface: A sailor is ordered to keep a lookout on the way back for lost people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns SEE (watch) into EES.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are not present where expected are missing, absent ones.

clue.text: Sporadic localities?

definitions.meaning: sporadic means scattered, occurring in various places
localities are places, this one and that one

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works as an adjective for scattered occurrence and literally as two place words, this place and that place.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scattered about, and literally pairs two words for places.

clue.text: Spanking vessels?

parts.note: smart, brisk ('spanking') sailing boats of a traditional single-masted fishing type, which also share their name with blows of a punishment

explanation.surface: It looks like it describes some fine, brisk boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanking' as an adjective means fine or brisk, but the answer also names slaps; the boats are traditional fishing craft of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional single-masted fishing boats bear this name, and it is also the word for slaps given as punishment.

clue.text: See chaps without fruit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the men surround the other piece

parts.note: chaps are men
lo is an old word meaning see or look

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at some men who have no fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'See' as LO is the archaic 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large round juicy fruit with a hard rind, such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Favourite comes round and takes part in the event

indicators.note: comes goes round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: a favourite is a pet

explanation.surface: The favourite turns up and joins in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' looks like arriving, but 'comes' is taken literally and 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a contest and vie with others is to take part in the event.

clue.text: Small party conflict

parts.note: a minor fight between small parties of troops

explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics or a celebration; here it is a small body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief, minor fight between small groups of soldiers is a limited engagement.

clue.text: Force regularly used on a group

definitions.text: Force regularly used on a group

parts.words: Force regularly used on a group
parts.note: the kind of force a lobbying body applies gives that body its name: a ___ group

explanation.surface: It sounds like a description of police tactics against a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like violence against a gathering, but the force meant is persuasion, the sort campaign bodies apply and are named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelling influence or force is the sense, and lobbying organisations are called after it.

clue.text: Students of the past?

parts.note: not historians but former students, the graduates of a school or university

explanation.surface: It reads as a description of historians, who study bygone times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Students of the past' suggests historians; here it means people who were students in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils or graduates of an institution are its old boys and girls, students who have left.

clue.text: It is a rich and varied source of charity

indicators.note: varied signals that the letters of it is a rich and are changed around

explanation.surface: Praise for a generous, diverse fund that supports good causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich and varied' reads as a stock phrase, but 'varied' is the anagram signal on 'It is a rich and'. The answer is a UK charity of the churches working against poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: A British church-backed relief and development agency is a well-known giver of charitable aid.

clue.text: About to fall from grace, by gum

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
to fall from grace is to commit sin

explanation.surface: Someone on the verge of a moral lapse exclaims 'by gum!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' looks like a mild oath; 'by' is only a link and 'gum' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky substance oozing from trees is gum, the classic natural example being pine sap.

clue.text: A new menu Thea provided for the club

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of menu Thea are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone called Thea has supplied a new set of dishes for a members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal working on 'menu Thea'; the 'A' at the front stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous gentlemen's club on Pall Mall in London bears this name, after the temple of the goddess Athena.

clue.text: Possibly she dreams it's a principal post

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of she dreams it's could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman perhaps fantasises about landing a top job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' is the anagram signal for 'she dreams it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman in charge of a school holds the post of principal, the senior teacher there.

clue.text: Service men who have a job to do

definitions.text: Service men who have a job to do

parts.words: Service men who have a job to do
parts.note: military personnel grouped together for one particular mission

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of armed forces formed for a specific operation is a body with one assigned mission.

clue.text: Tom rings, expressing disapproval

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the clue's surface; the answer is the plural noun for such jeers or the verb 'jeers at'

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to ring someone is to telephone, so rings means calls

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom keeps phoning to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a male cat; 'rings' is phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrill whistles or shouts from an audience convey displeasure, jeering at a performer.

clue.text: The rest of the players

parts.note: not the remaining players but the break or rest the players take midway through a match

explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' seems to mean the remainder; it is a break, the interval between halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval midway through a football match is when players get a rest.

clue.text: A hospital number

parts.note: 'number' read as numb-er: a hospital doctor who makes patients numb before surgery

explanation.surface: It looks like a patient's record reference or a ward phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as one who numbs; the specialist who puts patients under is such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor who administers drugs to deaden sensation before an operation is literally someone who numbs.

clue.text: Where children are to be found between two and five?

definitions.text: Where children are to be found between two and five?

parts.words: Where children are to be found between two and five?
parts.note: a day nursery for young children, typically aged two to five, rather than a time of day between two and five o'clock

explanation.surface: It sounds like asking where the kids are in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between two and five' suggests hours of the day; it means ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery where preschool children are minded is for kids of roughly that age range.

clue.text: Domestic service?

parts.note: not work as a servant but a service of crockery used at home: cups, saucers, pot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic service' suggests working as a servant; 'service' here is a set of matching crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of cups, saucers and pot is a china service used at home.

clue.text: Order ice after a place to eat is found

indicators.note: to order things is to put them in sequence, so the letters of ice after a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner orders ice cream once a restaurant has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like asking for food, but it is the anagram signal for 'ice after a'; 'is found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant, often in a workplace or college, is a place where people go to eat.

clue.text: Number in tour around royal house

indicators.note: in places the number inside the other letters
around suggests the letters of tour are turned about into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A count taken while touring a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TOUR into TUOR, and 'in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty of Henry VII, Henry VIII and Elizabeth I ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Actors perform foolishly in it

parts.note: a comic stage play full of silly, improbable antics by the cast

explanation.surface: A critic's sneer at actors behaving like idiots on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic drama built on absurd situations and buffoonery has its cast behave foolishly by design.

clue.text: Number with first-class ways to travel for landowners

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
A1 (written AI) means first-class, from the old shipping register rating
roads are ways to travel, abbreviated rds

explanation.surface: Estate owners enjoy plenty of luxurious ways of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, the first-class rating from Lloyd's Register of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a large estate is called by this title, a local word for lord.

clue.text: Private quarters

parts.note: not personal rooms but where an army private is housed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective meaning personal; it is the lowest army rank, and these are soldiers' lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers, including privates, are lodged in military buildings of this kind.

clue.text: Try to get aboard cutters

indicators.note: to get into the ship's letters means being placed inside them

parts.note: aboard means on a steamship, abbreviated SS, whose letters go round the other piece
to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to board some boats called cutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, steamship; 'to get' puts HEAR (try, as a judge tries a case) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Large scissors used for trimming hedges or fleece are cutting tools.

clue.text: He will be embraced by wildly ardent disciple

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside the other piece
wildly signals that the letters of ardent are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is hugged by an over-eager follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes ADRENT from the fodder, and 'will be embraced by' sets the 'He' inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or leader sticks to it, as a disciple does.
